I am an old woman here in Mulanje, and my strength is not what it used to be. This small piece of land, just a bit bigger than my yard, I plant beans together with maize like my mother taught me. I have no money for chemical fertilizer this season, but I keep a few chickens and I sweep their droppings and the ash from my cooking fire onto the plot. The seeds I save from last year's harvest — they are my own beans, the ones that grow well here even when the rains are poor.
